$comment: Coverage baseline (DR-5, task 009). Captured from 3 green CI runs of the
RUN_EVALS-off `test-mcp` "Coverage-instrumented suite" step on
feat/wave-s-enforcement-substrate — see `runIds` (provenance the ratchet
validates) and `sourceRuns` (per-run detail) below.
`metrics.*.pct` is the baseline percentage, taken from the LATEST of the
three runs (29624088763, commit 0d91a8bd — the final tree at this task's
dispatch tip; its coverage is slightly higher than the two earlier runs
because the DR-10 fix added a test covering the degrade path).
`metrics.*.spread` is the measured max-min PCT spread of that metric across
all 3 runs — real, unpadded variance, not a guess.
`metrics.*.epsilon` is `max(spread, 0.1)` (the 0.1-percentage-point floor),
recorded here for human/audit visibility ONLY: tools/audit/gates/check-coverage-ratchet.mjs
re-derives this value itself at comparison time from `spread` and NEVER reads
a pre-baked epsilon field, so a baseline that (incorrectly) recorded a zero or
understated epsilon can never disarm the ratchet. See that script's header for
the full fail-closed provenance contract this file must satisfy (non-empty
`runIds` + a numeric `spread` per metric).
All 4 metrics measured a sub-floor spread (0.03-0.04pp) on this feature
branch's 3 runs, so the 0.1pp floor governs every metric's epsilon verbatim —
none of the measured spreads exceeded it.

laneConfig.RUN_EVALS: unset — the "Coverage-instrumented suite (DR-5, RUN_EVALS pinned off)" step in .github/workflows/ci.yml's test-mcp job sets `env.RUN_EVALS: ''`, overriding the job-level derivation from `needs.changes.outputs.prompts`, so the measured lane never varies with prompts-touching PRs.
